In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DOC accumulation in the Mediterranean Sea is not related to the high N:P ratio, but to the low chlorophyll concentration and low phosphate availability.
the DOC accumulation is a consequence of a high N:P ratio, which is a characteristic of the Mediterranean Sea and not a consequence of the low chlorophyll levels.

the accumulation of DOC in LPLC area is a direct result of a combination of factors including: the high nutrient availability (N and Si), the low chlorophyll (low phytoplankton biomass), the low phosphate (high N:P ratio), the high bacterial production (high heterotrophic bacterial biomass) and the high temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the accumulation of DOC in the Mediterranean Sea is not a consequence of a lack of remineralizers (as it is usually believed) but is a result of an imbalance between primary producers and remineralizers.

The main takeaway from our work is that
DOC accumulation can be a direct result of the bottom up control exerted by the nutrient limitation of osmotroph growth.
DOC dynamics in the Mediterranean Sea are not only controlled by the N:P ratio of phytoplankton, but also by the bottom up control on osmotrophs.
